correctness.rationale: The unitary Fourier transform yields exact spectrum N|ĝ(k)|²; every profile is positive so bounds are defined. Reflection makes equal powers improve both extrema. For r<R, the short arc supplies an index with both spectral distances no larger (one strictly smaller) than the antipodal maximizing pair, while the long arc supplies both distances no smaller (one strictly larger) than its minimizing pair. This proves simultaneous strict extrema ordering for every even N, including N=2 vacuously. At antipodal gap, reflected eigenvalues force a strict worsening for nonzero power imbalance. Heat multipliers e^{-4t}e^{4t cos(2πk/N)} yield exact parity-dependent cosh extrema. The quantified strict robustness margins follow from explicit eigenvalues. A standalone checker passed 161085 supplementary assertions; computation is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: All finite translated two-channel Gabor acquisition systems with strictly radial decreasing energy share a single exactly optimal frequency design, irrespective of the shape or scale of the window. Exact lower/upper frame bounds govern noise amplification and optimal reconstruction stability, a different, motivated objective from frame potential. The graph-heat specialization provides new explicit t- and parity-sensitive bounds, a universal design and strict quantitative penalties for gaps and power imbalance. The domain is a broad natural spectral class, and the two-arc strictness theorem supplies a structural tool rather than a formal parameter substitution.
